gloss: bamboo fence — a traditional Japanese garden fence made from bamboo culms or split bamboo strips

definitions.gloss: a fence made of bamboo, especially the traditional decorative or functional bamboo fences used in Japanese gardens, temples, and around traditional houses
definitions.explanation: A fence constructed from bamboo culms ({竹|たけ} "bamboo" + {垣|かき} "fence, hedge"). {竹垣|たけがき} is closely associated with traditional Japanese gardens, tea-house grounds, and temple compounds, where it serves both as a boundary marker and as an aesthetic element. There are many named styles distinguished by how the bamboo is cut, woven, or bound — for example {建仁寺垣|けんにんじがき} (vertical split-bamboo panels), {四|よ}つ{目垣|めがき} (open lattice), and {御簾垣|みすがき} (horizontal slatted style). Modern uses include both authentic bamboo and synthetic look-alikes used in suburban gardens.

examples.japanese: {庭|にわ}に{低|ひく}い{竹垣|たけがき}を{巡|めぐ}らせた。
examples.english: I put a low bamboo fence around the garden.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}いお{寺|てら}の{境内|けいだい}は、{苔|こけ}むした{竹垣|たけがき}で{囲|かこ}まれていた。
examples.english: The grounds of the old temple were surrounded by a moss-covered bamboo fence.

examples.japanese: {京都|きょうと}の{町家|まちや}の{庭|にわ}には、{建仁寺垣|けんにんじがき}と{呼|よ}ばれる{竹垣|たけがき}がよく{使|つか}われている。
examples.english: In the gardens of Kyoto townhouses, a kind of bamboo fence called kenninji-gaki is often used.

notes:
{竹垣|たけがき} is a fence made of bamboo, strongly associated with traditional Japanese gardens and architecture. The compound is {竹|たけ} (bamboo) + {垣|かき} (fence/hedge), with rendaku turning {かき} into がき.

CONSTRUCTION:
- Vertical bamboo culms or split-bamboo strips bound to a horizontal frame
- Often tied with black palm-fiber rope ({棕櫚縄|しゅろなわ}) for visual contrast
- May be solid (for screening) or open-lattice (for partial visibility)

COMMON STYLES (NAMED VARIETIES):
- {建仁寺垣|けんにんじがき}: solid panel of vertical split bamboo, named after Kennin-ji temple in Kyoto
- {四|よ}つ{目垣|めがき}: open square-lattice style; common in tea gardens
- {御簾垣|みすがき}: horizontal slatted style resembling a bamboo blind
- {大津垣|おおつがき}: woven horizontal-and-vertical style
- {鉄砲垣|てっぽうがき}: alternating wide bamboo culms on opposite sides of a horizontal pole
- {竜安寺垣|りょうあんじがき}: low decorative style at Ryoan-ji temple

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {竹垣|たけがき}を{作|つく}る: to build a bamboo fence
- {竹垣|たけがき}を{結|ゆ}う: to tie/construct a bamboo fence (using rope)
- {竹垣|たけがき}を{巡|めぐ}らせる: to put a bamboo fence around (a property)
- {竹垣|たけがき}で{囲|かこ}む: to surround with a bamboo fence
- {竹垣|たけがき}{越|ご}しに: across/over a bamboo fence
- {人工|じんこう}{竹垣|たけがき}: artificial bamboo fence (synthetic resin)

SIMILAR / RELATED TERMS:
- {生|い}け{垣|がき}: a hedge made of living plants — different material, similar function
- {板垣|いたがき}: a fence made of wooden boards
- {柵|さく}: fence in general, including wire and metal fences
- {塀|へい}: a wall or solid fence (often plaster, concrete, or brick)
- {籬|まがき}: a literary/poetic word for a low rustic fence (often bamboo or brushwood)
- {竹林|ちくりん}: a bamboo grove (the source of the material)

CULTURAL CONTEXT:
- An iconic feature of Japanese garden ({日本庭園|にほんていえん}) design
- Different temples and tea houses developed distinctive styles, many of which now bear the temple's name
- Maintenance is a traditional craft; bamboo fences weather and need replacement every several years
